issues.title: Huge pages for large join tables v2: HJ pointer table >=8MB + perfect-HJ slot arrays
issues.hypothesis: E0038 (THP-backed HJ pointer table for tables >=32MB) just missed acceptance. q09 came in at -7.0% against a noise threshold of 8.6%; implementer runs gave q09 -8.4/-15/-9.3%, q03 -3..-13% and q08 -8%, with nothing slower once free-time DONTNEED+NOHUGEPAGE was added. At 32MB the threshold left the second big random-access join in q09 on 4KB pages. That is the (ps_partkey,ps_suppkey) HJ: build 435K rows, 1M slots = 8MB pointer table, probed 3.27M times, 0.49s of q09's 2.65s CPU. An 8MB table is beyond the 4KB-page L2 TLB reach (~6MB), so every probe costs a TLB miss plus a page walk. The same applies to perfect-HJ slot_to_row/build_bits arrays sized to the key range (perfect_hash_join_executor.cpp:158/162). q13's RIGHT perfect HJ over 1.5M customers uses a 12MB slot_to_row array, and the sparse perfect HJs in q07/q02 behave the same way. Huge pages for every random-access join table of 8MB or more should push q09 well past its noise and add gains on q03/q08/q13.
issues.plan: 1) Re-apply E0038 in src/execution/join_hashtable.cpp as described in the ledger. Allocate through BufferAllocator with 2MB slack and align `entries` to 2MB. Call madvise(MADV_HUGEPAGE) before InitializePointerTable, only when /sys/kernel/mm/transparent_hugepage/enabled is [madvise] or [always]. PointerTableUsableSize() handles non-power-of-two padded sizes. On free, in the destructor, Reset() and the grow path, call MADV_DONTNEED then MADV_NOHUGEPAGE; this step is mandatory, or q02 gets 5-9% slower. 2) Lower the threshold from 32MB to 8MB (1M slots). 3) Factor the align+madvise+cleanup logic into a small static helper or RAII struct in join_hashtable.cpp, or a new common header. Use it in PerfectHashJoinExecutor (src/execution/operator/join/perfect_hash_join_executor.cpp:158-162, and slot_found_match at 297/418) when an array is >=8MB, in place of make_unsafe_uniq_array. 4) Measure q09, q16, q03 and q02 alone several times each before the full bench. Watch q16 in particular: its table is 8MB with 296K build rows, and it swung -14..+7% at a 4MB threshold. If q16 is slower beyond its noise, gate on build rows >= 400K instead.
issues.generality: Any hash join whose build exceeds ~250K rows, or any perfect HJ over a key range of 1M or more. That covers FK joins against fact tables and large dimensions. Small joins are untouched. A query with a mid-size build that runs only once may pay THP fault/compaction cost.
issues.risk: Medium-low. Memory is tracked by the same allocator. The main hazard is huge-page state leaking into recycled jemalloc memory, which the free-time cleanup handles. q16 is borderline at the 8MB threshold.

dispatch: Huge pages for large join tables v2: HJ pointer table >=8MB + perfect-HJ slot arrays

## Memory (gen3)

## State
- gen1: accepted JoinDependent rule order (q19), contains() selectivity (q09), perfect HJ RIGHT (q13), BF first key multi-key HJ (q09), key-set range filter through compress projs (q18), exact bitmap BF, semi-join estimate, OR-of-ranges mask, FSST simple decode + substring prefilter (q13), DELIM_GET-build BF (q22). Best 1.281x.
- gen2: E0021 deliminate SEMI + exact BF through CM offset; E0022 exact-BF small-range floor; E0023 ANTI deliminator; E0024 parallel perfect-HJ build; E0027 BitPacking per-value select + exact BF 2^27; E0029 sparse perfect-HJ exact BF; E0031 block cache 256MB + large perfect HA v3 (q13 -25%). Best 1.800x.
- gen2 r16: E0032 rare-pair substring search RETIRED (q13 -4%; FSST decode dominates). Bundle only with a decode-side gain.
- gen3 r1: E0033 clustered-key radix agg ACCEPTED (q18 -13.6%). Best 1.824x.
- gen3 r2: E0034 partition-staged sink into the shared perfect HA ACCEPTED (q13 -15..-17%). Best 1.860x.
- gen3 r3: E0035 parallel HJ finalize for 64K-1M row builds ACCEPTED (geomean -8.5%). Best 2.028x.
- gen3 r4: E0036 streaming run agg for interior rows of the clustered-key agg ACCEPTED (q18 466→239ms). Best 2.120x.
- gen3 r5: E0037 partition-local slot addressing for HJ finalize RETIRED (noise; 16 partitions still give 8MB regions, so the working set is not smaller).
- gen3 r6: E0038 THP HJ pointer table >=32MB RETIRED as a NEAR MISS. Bench q09 -7.0% (threshold 8.6%); implementer runs gave q09 -8..-15%, q03 -3..-13%, q08 -8%, geomean -0.5..-1.8%. It was a good idea, just too narrow.
- gen3 r7: DISPATCHED THP v2. Same as E0038 plus an 8MB threshold (covers q09's partsupp HJ, 1M slots) plus perfect-HJ slot arrays of 8MB or more. If it is retired again for q16 at 8MB, retry with a build-row gate.
- Backlog issues.md entries "Length-aware selectivity", "Perfect HJ RIGHT", "Join min/max+BF through CM", "Large perfect HA v3" have ALL LANDED (stale); "RIGHT_SEMI/ANTI join filters" was part of E0021. Do not dispatch them.
- Claude auto-memory (~/.claude/.../memory) holds results from a PREVIOUS evolve run. Treat them as strong priors.

## THP facts (E0038)
- THP on this machine: enabled=[madvise], defrag=[madvise]. Readable via read_csv('/sys/...', header=false, columns={'a':'VARCHAR'}, delim='|').
- Free-time MADV_DONTNEED + MADV_NOHUGEPAGE is REQUIRED. Without it, recycled jemalloc memory keeps the huge-page flag and q02 is +5..9%.
- With a 4MB threshold, q16 (8MB table, 296K rows) swung -14..+7%.
- Padded allocation: the size is not a power of two, so PointerTableUsableSize can detect it.

## Profiling trick (works, cheap)
- In one dbe-tool sql call: warm up twice, then `PRAGMA enable_profiling='json'; PRAGMA profiling_output='/tmp/x.json';` <query>; `PRAGMA disable_profiling;` and then
  `SELECT unnest(regexp_extract_all(content, '"operator_name": "([^"]*)"|"operator_timing": ([0-9.e-]+)|"operator_cardinality": ([0-9]+)')) FROM read_text('/tmp/x.json');`
  Each operator's timing and cardinality come BEFORE its name, in pre-order (probe child first).
- The profile.md plan for q09 is a COLD run. Always re-profile hot.
- dbe-tool rejects shell variables and `;` chains with other commands. `| tail`, `| cut` and `| grep -v` work.
- Forcing join order: `SET disabled_optimizers='join_order,build_side_probe_side'` with explicit JOIN ... ON nesting (left = probe).

## Hot CPU breakdowns
- q09 (2.65s user, 364ms): HJ o_orderkey=l_orderkey 0.80s (build 3.27M, probe 2.94M); lineitem scan 0.57s; HJ (ps_partkey,ps_suppkey) 0.49s (build 435K, probe 3.27M); agg 0.19s; part scan 0.14s.
- q03 (1.08s user): lineitem scan 0.38s; HJ l_orderkey 0.38s (build 1.45M orders, probe 301.8K); orders scan + customer HJ 0.31s.
- q07 (~165ms): HJ o_orderkey=l_orderkey 0.287s (build 1.46M, probe 100.8K); lineitem scan 0.47s; lineitem⋈supplier HJ 0.13s.
- q05 (r7, 150ms): lineitem scan 0.33s (1.82M out, BF from orders); HJ l_orderkey 0.31s (build 455K orders⋈customer); top HJ (l_suppkey,c_nationkey)=(s_suppkey,s_nationkey) 0.12s, build = UNFILTERED supplier 100K, out 72.6K; orders scan 0.125s. TESTED: a forced order with supplier⋈nation(EUROPE) as the build gave no gain (146-168 vs 145-173ms). Don't pursue q05 join order.
- Build-only micro: 9.1M build rows = 1.34s user + 0.42s sys (page faults on a 256MB table, fresh mmap); ~104ns per build row.
- q18 (239ms, 1.85s CPU): subquery HASH_GROUP_BY 1.17s CPU over 60M rows / 15M groups. The cost is per GROUP (~70ns), not per row. CM compress 0.19s, orders scan 0.14s.
- HJ pointer table: capacity = NextPowerOfTwo(count*2.0) (join_hashtable.hpp:417), 8B entries; BufferAllocator at join_hashtable.cpp:~804/812.

## Refuted (don't retry)
- Compacting sparse scan chunks before an HJ probe.
- VARCHAR low-cardinality group key in q09: ≤0.07s.
- Partition-local HJ slots (E0037).
- q05 filtered-supplier join order.

## q18 facts
- q03's clustered proof fails: sparse join output chunks span row groups.
- Next q18 idea: cut the per-group cost of the streaming run path (finalize from the arena instead of a ColumnDataCollection run store?). See radix_partitioned_hashtable.cpp SinkInteriorRuns (~947).

## HJ / perfect facts
- physical_hash_join.cpp:388 PARALLEL_CONSTRUCT_THRESHOLD = 64K. `PRAGMA verify_parallelism` forces parallel finalize.
- Perfect HJ arrays: perfect_hash_join_executor.cpp:158 build_bits, 162 slot_to_row, 297/418 slot_found_match (make_unsafe_uniq_array).
- Perfect HA: perfect_aggregate_hashtable.cpp:13-75 (lazy_init owned_data, staging per stripe); plan_aggregate.cpp:141-299; physical_perfecthash_aggregate.cpp.

## q13 (319ms)
- orders scan + NOT LIKE 1.60-1.9s CPU, mostly FSST decode. RIGHT perfect HJ 0.30s. Compress projection 0.23s. Perfect HA 0.49s (already staged per stripe).

## Acceptance lessons
- Acceptance needs BOTH: some template faster beyond its noise AND an improved visible geomean. Any template slower beyond noise retires the issue.
- Bundling or widening a near-miss works (E0021, E0027, E0029, E0031).
- Fixed "small → single-thread" thresholds hid big serial phases (E0035).
- Full-bench single-template outliers of ±8..29% happen; rerun alone.

## Codebase facts
- Perfect HJ BF: CanUseBloomFilter + PushPerfectHashJoinBloomFilters (physical_hash_join.cpp); FillExactBloomFilter.
- HJ BF filled in JoinHashTable::InsertHashes during Finalize.
- `SET disabled_optimizers='join_filter_pushdown'` for A/B.
- BitPacking Select ~bitpacking.cpp:886. TEMP tables are never compressed (their plans differ).
- Substring prefilter: column_segment.cpp:662-860. CM: src/optimizer/compressed_materialization*. Deliminator: deliminator.cpp. Join filters: join_filter_pushdown_optimizer.cpp.
- jemalloc oversize_threshold is 256MB. block_allocator.cpp:72-77 uses madvise.

## How to measure
- Micro A/B: several statements in one dbe-tool sql call, `.timer on` on the first line; the first run is cold.
- Bench noise: q16 ~7.9%, q18 ~5%, q13 ~14%, q09 ~8.6%, q14 ~5.1%, q05 ~20%, q04 ~20%, q07 ~13%.

## Profile snapshot (gen3 r7): q09 386, q13 326, q18 237, q03 184, q16 164, q07 156, q05 149, q08 128, q04 128, q17 114, q14 107, q19 94, q22 94, q02 57.

## Dead / exhausted
- CM join-key removal, HJ prefetch, agg run-collapse, in-place finalize, FSST heap reuse, dictionary filter, scan filter cost ordering, early HT grow, sparse perfect HJ (8M range), hashed BF through CM offset, q13 eager aggregation, fused hashed BF probe, allocator flush thresholds, substring search alone (E0032), private-table staging for perfect HA, scan chunk compaction, partition-local HJ slots, q05 join order.

## Next candidates
1. THP v2 (dispatched r7). If accepted, extend THP to large GroupedAggregateHashTable entries (aggregate_hashtable.cpp:~290) with the same cleanup.
2. q18 per-group streaming-run overhead (~70ns/group, 1.17s CPU).
3. q09 multi-key HJ probe at ~120ns per match.
4. q08 hot profile not taken yet.
5. q13: skip the unused local-table alloc (backlog, low gain).
